structured_output.summary:
The most useful outside evidence is on H3.2 (progressive resizing). Fable's record CIFAR-10 airbench recipe (fulcrumresearch/cifar-10-speedrun, 1.83 s at 94%) gets its biggest single gain from a three-stage curriculum: one third of epochs each at 24, 28 and 32 px. Low-res inputs are made by bilinearly downsampling the full 32 px image, then a global max pool. The whole run is captured as one CUDA graph with fused foreach optimizer ops, so a 24 px epoch costs 0.575x a 32 px epoch. With plain torch.compile it costs about 0.65x. E008's 16% saving for 50% of steps at 24 px implies about 0.68x, so some resolution-independent overhead is still there. Fable's investigation puts the cost of the 24 px start at about 0.12 pp on CIFAR-10, repaid with about +0.45 epochs. E008 spent 50% of steps at 24 px and lost 0.55 pp, so a 24/28/32-by-thirds schedule plus about 0.5-1 extra epoch is a better-grounded next test than 50% at 24 px.

Fable's other settings: batch 1536, SGD momentum 0.825, label smoothing 0.09, translate 2 with reflect padding, an LR floor of 0.05 with an EMA tail, SiLU, and orthogonalized (Muon-style) momentum on conv filters. Hiverge's 1.98 s record also switched GELU to SiLU, computed whitening by SVD and added brightness/contrast augmentation.

The airbench paper's ablations rank BN-bias LR scaling (bias_scaler 64) as a large epoch saver: 18 to 13.5 epochs on CIFAR-10. The legacy airbench96 hyperparameters (lr 9.0, momentum 0.85, wd 0.012, whiten_bias_epochs 3, LS 0.2, translate 4, cutout 12, tta_level 2) are worth checking against the arena recipe. airbench96 reaches 79.3% on CIFAR-100 without cutout on a long schedule, so the wide net has about 4 pp of headroom above 0.753. That fits E009's finding that the narrow net's ceiling is the problem.

The futurebiohackers PR, which is the source for H1.1, is now deleted (404). Search snippets give its recipe as LS 0.3, lr 9.0, wd 0.012, 8.5 epochs, reaching 75.29% in 8.11 s. That is about 2.3 pp above E001's 73.0% at the same epochs. Whether it used TTA can't be checked; TTA is illegal here. I found no published CIFAR-100 speedrun leaderboard entries beyond the organizers' 59.3 s ResNet9 baseline.

findings.claim: The record CIFAR-10 airbench-family recipe uses res_schedule [24,24,24,28,28,28,32,32,32] (one entry per epoch, 8.875 epochs total). Low-res inputs come from F.interpolate(bilinear) inside the compiled step. A global max pool (x.flatten(2).max(2)) replaces MaxPool2d(3). The entire ~284-step run is captured as one CUDA graph, with per-step LR scalars precomputed into a CUDA table and the optimizer fused into compiled torch._foreach_* ops.
findings.relevance: Gives a concrete alternative to E008's 50%-at-24 px schedule. That schedule spends only a third at 24 px and finishes the last third at full resolution, where the BN stats and features re-adapt.

findings.claim: Downsampling the full image, rather than cropping a 24 px window, is what makes the 24 px start pay. The 24 px start costs about 0.0012 accuracy and is repaid with about +0.45 epochs, for a net -0.08 s at n=200. A 24 px epoch costs 0.575x a 32 px epoch under a whole-run CUDA graph (theory 0.5625) but about 0.65x steady-state under plain torch.compile, because of resolution-independent overhead (eager foreach optimizer, loader work). Adding 28->32 was worth -0.128 s and extending it to 24->28->32 a further -0.081 s.
findings.relevance: E008 saved 16% with 50% of steps at 24 px, which implies a 24 px step of about 0.68x, close to the plain-compile figure. Moving the optimizer into the graph would raise the resize payoff. The accuracy cost is bought back with extra epochs, so the useful test is resize + extra epochs against E004, not resize at equal epochs.

findings.claim: Progressive resizing (24 -> 28 -> 32 px) was the largest single gain in Fable's 1.828 s CIFAR-10 record (from 1.978 s). 'Small images carry less signal, so the curriculum needs a slightly longer schedule ... but each early step is much cheaper.' Precomputing the augmented batch stream outside the timed region was flagged as specification gaming.
findings.relevance: Supports keeping H3.2 open despite E008's inconclusive result. Also a rule reminder: augmentation must happen in the timed prepare/train.

findings.claim: Other champion settings: batch_size 1536, sgd_momentum 0.825, label_smoothing 0.09, translate 2 with reflect padding, linear decay to an LR floor of 0.05 with an EMA/lookahead tail (ema_every 4, decay 0.7), BN momentum about 0.557 (PyTorch convention), SiLU, and frozen 2x2 whitening with a briefly trained bias.
findings.relevance: The record recipe uses weaker translate (2 vs 4) and LS of about 0.1, consistent with E004 (removing cutout and setting LS 0.1 gave +1.26 pp). Suggests testing translate 2 and batch 1536 at this scale.

findings.claim: Hiverge's 1.98 s CIFAR-10 record changes over airbench (2.59 s): vectorized/batched Muon updates, compiled forward+backward, GELU -> SiLU, whitening computed by SVD instead of eigendecomposition, a random brightness/contrast augmentation, and re-tuned steps, LRs and momentum. It also used selective TTA, which is illegal in this task.
findings.relevance: A cheap activation swap (GELU -> SiLU) and a new augmentation to try. No per-change numbers are given, so the expected effect size is unknown.

findings.claim: Ablations on CIFAR-10 epochs-to-94%: whitening init halves time (to 21 epochs). Dirac init: 21 -> 18 epochs. BN-bias LR scaling: 18 -> 13.5 epochs, the largest single step after whitening. Lookahead: 13.5 -> 12. Multi-crop TTA: 12 -> 10.8. Alternating flip: final 9.9 epochs. On CIFAR-100, airbench96 reaches 79.27% without cutout and 79.76% with cutout (long schedule), 1.7 pp above ResNet-18.
findings.relevance: The wide 128/384/5xx net has about 4 pp of ceiling above 0.753, unlike the narrow net (E009). Bias scaling is a big sample-efficiency lever; check the arena recipe has bias_scaler=64 on BN biases. This also gives prior evidence for H1.3 (whitening/dirac matter a lot on CIFAR-10).

findings.claim: airbench96 hyperparameters: train_epochs 37, batch 1024, lr 9.0, momentum 0.85, weight_decay 0.012, bias_scaler 64, label_smoothing 0.2, whiten_bias_epochs 3, flip + translate 4 + cutout 12, scaling_factor 1/9, tta_level 2. BN has eps 1e-12, a frozen weight and a trainable bias. LR: 10% warmup from 0.2 to 1.0, then linear decay to 0. Lookahead alpha schedule 0.95**5*(t/T)**3, applied every 5 steps.
findings.relevance: Reference for confirming the arena recipe matches airbench96 (bias scaler, whiten-bias epochs, lookahead schedule). These were tuned for 37 epochs, not about 10, so the warmup fraction, momentum and lookahead cadence are candidates for H4 re-tuning.

findings.source: https://github.com/abdullah-athar/iterate-futurebiohackers/pull/3 (search snippet only; PR and repo now return 404)
findings.claim: According to search snippets, the futurebiohackers recipe is 3-conv groups with widths 128/384/576, label smoothing 0.3, lr 9.0, wd 0.012 and 8.5 epochs, chosen from about 40 configs swept on Modal A100-SXM4. It reports 75.29% (one config 75.5%) in 8.11 s. Whether TTA was used cannot be checked because the source is deleted.
findings.relevance: Conflicts with E001 (73.0% at 8.5 epochs with LS 0.2 + cutout, no TTA): about 2.3 pp unexplained. The likely cause is TTA in their eval (airbench96 default tta_level 2), which is illegal here. H1.1's 'without TTA' premise should be treated as unverified, and LS 0.3 should not be taken as evidence against E004's LS 0.1.

findings.claim: The organizers' verified A100 baseline is a ResNet9-style net, 40 epochs, width 64: 75.36% mean accuracy, 59.30 s mean prepare+train, 0.117 s inference. The L40 calibration (50 trials) had an accuracy std of 0.25 pp. No competitor submissions are public.
findings.relevance: Per-seed sd of about 0.25 pp gives a 3-seed mean sd of about 0.15 pp, consistent with the notebook's noise estimate. Our E004 (8.94 s) is already about 6.6x faster than baseline; there is no public CIFAR-100 record to beat or copy.

findings.claim: airbench96_faster: the proxy net (32/64/64, depth 2) scores every 1024-example batch, and the main net (128/384/512, depth 3) backprops only the top 512 by loss. Settings: 45 epochs, lr 9.0, LS 0.2, TTA level 2. It reaches 96.00% in 27.3 s on CIFAR-10, tuned for a long schedule.
findings.relevance: Filtering was shown only in a 45-epoch, over-fitting regime on CIFAR-10. At about 10 epochs on CIFAR-100, where the model under-fits and is step-limited (E007/E009 post-mortems), dropping half of each batch probably costs more accuracy than it saves. That lowers the prior on H3.1.1.
